correctness.rationale: The nested cut decomposition yields an exact norm formula for any nonnegative unit-mass barycenter, including the correct source/target Gini normalization. Uniform weights give the Hilbert value; p>2 force balance and subadditivity of x^alpha with alpha=(p-2)/(p-1) imply all Jacobian weights <=1/2, and a two-extreme input attains the resulting sharp cut ratio locally. For p<2, the nonlinear center is monotone and translation equivariant so the full Gini ratio is <=2; an explicit perturbation at a datum equal to the center gives c_h/h->1 and hence the ratio ->2. Finite rational cut checks and nonlinear root checks passed but are not treated as proofs.

originality.rationale: Kyng et al. (2015) supply a sup-norm perturbation bound for graph lex-minimizing extensions, and Marano et al. (2002) analyze convergence of finite p-best approximants. Neither inspected statement yields the sharp two-input complete-pair Gini coefficient for the variational p-center. A related star p-harmonic result formulated with leaf/edge Lipschitz seminorms uses different input/output seminorms and has identical nonquadratic constants, so it does not imply the new Gini distinction between p<2 and p>2. Published record searches found neighboring but not covering claims. Residual priority risk persists.
residual_risks: Priority search cannot exclude unindexed treatments of Gini or complete-graph total variation under nonlinear barycenter insertion.

value.rationale: The complete-pair Gini variation is a natural dispersion and robust-label metric distinct from sup and edge-Lipschitz norms. Its sharp two-input extension coefficient splits into genuinely different subquadratic, Hilbert, and superquadratic regimes, whereas the nearest known sup-norm law does not detect the split. The classification holds for all star sizes and all real exponents and supplies explicit sharpness mechanisms, giving usable constants for nonlinear graph interpolation sensitivity.
